     1	# Statement ledger
     2	
     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision 975feb3, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98 and 3920258.
     9	The later revisions changed prose, titles, the literature review, layout and
    10	figures, added a zero-covariance remark after `H:homog` and qualified a strict
    11	comparison in `T:first` (not cited here) as asserted only for nonzero
    12	covariance. Every cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at
    13	3920258 and 975feb3. Between these two revisions every cited lemma,
    14	proposition, theorem and equation has the same statement and proof up to
    15	whitespace and braces, with one exception: the statement of `T:full-upper`
    16	(cited only as not formalized) now ends with a cross-reference to Theorem
    17	`T:intro-upper` instead of Goal `G:upper`, and its mathematics is unchanged.
    18	The cited sections `S:model` (the zero-covariance remark and a roadmap
    19	figure), `S:two-clock-screen` (Goal `G:sharp` renamed Theorem
    20	`T:intro-second-moment` in the prose), `S:temporal-equilibrium` and
    21	`S:intrinsic-white-evaluation` (new attribution paragraphs) changed only in
    22	prose. TeX line numbers were moved to 975feb3 by a line map; each cited range
    23	lies in unchanged text (script checks recorded in
    24	`provenance/manuscript-anchor.json`).
    25	
    26	## Scope
    27	
    28	- The "What it states" column is a faithful paraphrase, sometimes
    29	  shortened. The exact statement is the Lean type in
    30	  `StratonovichHAMAudit/<Module>.lean`; `Audit/<module>/` prints the
    31	  elaborated types.
    32	- The rows cover every public theorem (1430) and 301 definitions whose
    33	  values are stated as facts or that name a manuscript object. The other 70
    34	  public definitions have no rows of their own: 66 (for example `kappa`,
    35	  `delta`, `gauge`, `counts`, `InventoryProduct.partialEval` and
    36	  `OccupationPhysicalClass.volI`) only name quantities or measures used in
    37	  those statements, and four are the instances that make
    38	  `TimeCompletion.Pre` a pre-inner-product space; read their bodies in the
    39	  Lean source or in `Audit/`.
    40	- The `StratonovichHAMAudit` modules check finite, algebraic and scalar
    41	  steps only: exact identities, polynomial and rational certificates,
    42	  real-power bookkeeping, parameter ranges, and a few finite-dimensional
    43	  inner-product and finite-word facts.
    44	- The fifty-five `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment` modules (sections marked
    45	  "whole result" below; four of them are the wave-kernel and time-fractional
    46	  foundation of `ClockCopy`, `GaussianTest` is the Gaussian-test foundation
    47	  of `MaskedSpectralGrowth`, and `VariationalFloor`, `SpatialFourierBound`
    48	  and `SeriesType` are foundations added in wave L6, `H1Density` one added
    49	  in wave L7) model `H:homog` and formalize the conclusions of forty-three
    50	  labelled results, to the scopes specified below (some with a narrower
    51	  conclusion, stated per result). Thirty-eight need no supplied input:
    52	  `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` is stated with the manuscript's own hypotheses.
    53	  `L:gram-scalar-algebra` and `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` are proved under weaker
    54	  hypotheses (no completeness or `C_ij >= 0`; no `delta < 1`) and also
    55	  stated exactly as the manuscript does by the wrappers
    56	  `gram_scalar_algebra_paper` and `rayleigh_tail_paper`; the Rayleigh
    57	  lemma's "In particular" application to another proposition is not
    58	  formalized. `E:kappa` and `E:driver-parameters` are proved from the
    59	  numerical part of `H:homog` (a generalization) and also restated under the
    60	  full hypothesis `H:homog`, which `HomogHypothesis.HomogCovariance` models
    61	  clause by clause (covariance measure, spectral measure, evenness,
    62	  temperedness, positive-definiteness, scaling, parameter ranges).
    63	  `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` and `L:temporal-equilibrium` are stated with
    64	  the manuscript's own hypotheses (`gamma_beta_paper`,
    65	  `temporal_equilibrium_paper`). The finite slice of `S:compact-gaussian`,
    66	  `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    67	  `R:gaussian-one-variance-test`, is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses
    68	  (independent standard Gaussians on an arbitrary probability space) on top
    69	  of a finite Gaussian integration-by-parts foundation (`GaussianIBP`).
    70	  `L:variational-control-dilation` is stated with the section's hypotheses
    71	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
    72	  `variational_control_dilation_paper`, for the cost in its integral form
    73	  and the rate defined by the real Rayleigh supremum
    74	  `E:variational-real-rayleigh` (over a weak-gradient `H^1(R^d)` built in
    75	  `WeakSobolev`, since Mathlib has no Sobolev spaces); the identifications
    76	  with `E W(Psi)^2` and `sqrt(-E_s)` are not formalized.
    77	  `P:masked-spectral-growth` is stated with the section's hypotheses
    78	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_spectral_growth_paper`, and the
    79	  homogeneity of the spectral measure, which the TeX derives in the proof of
    80	  `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`, is derived from `H:homog`
    81	  (`spectralHomogeneous_of_homog`). Hence `P:clock-copy-obstruction` and the
    82	  finiteness part of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (with `N_2(theta)^2 >= 0`)
    83	  are stated with nothing supplied by the `ClockCopyHomog` wrappers. The
    84	  rest of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (`N_0`, the scaling identities, the
    85	  tails `E:damped-tail-norms`, and the smoothing and truncation sentence
    86	  read as a multiplier `g` in `[0,1]` on the spectral measure and a
    87	  restriction of the Laplace variable to a measurable set) is
    88	  `DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper`, for an arbitrary family
    89	  `G` with the mass identity `GreenMass G` as hypothesis, and is stated with
    90	  `H:homog` alone (no `Gamma != 0`) and nothing supplied by
    91	  `WaveGreen.damped_homogeneous_norms_wave`: `WaveGreen` builds the wave
    92	  Green measures `G_s` for `d = 1, 2, 3` (in `d = 3` with Mathlib's
    93	  `Measure.toSphere` taken as the surface measure, a definitional choice)
    94	  and proves their mass `G_s(R^d) = s`, finiteness, support in the closed
    95	  radius-`s` ball and the scaling `G_s(sA) = sG_1(A)`.
    96	  `L:masked-time-completion` is stated with the manuscript's hypotheses (`0
    97	  < a < 1`, `T > 0`; no `Gamma != 0`) by `masked_time_completion_paper`: the
    98	  completion `H_a` is built (`TimeCompletion`, Mathlib's completion of
    99	  `L^2(0,T)` under the temporal form, over `C`), with positive
   100	  semidefiniteness, separability, the continuous extension, the complexified
   101	  norm identity, interval amplitudes, and density of the real compact smooth
   102	  tests on `(0,T)`. `E:masked-time-schur` and `L:masked-temporal-modulation`
   103	  are stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by `time_schur_paper` and
   104	  `masked_temporal_modulation_paper` for the defining double integral, and
   105	  `E:masked-time-schur` also for the norm of `H_a` (`emb_norm_sq_le`).
   106	  `L:masked-trig-products` and `L:masked-continuous-wave` are stated in this
   107	  `H_a` with the manuscript's hypotheses and nothing supplied
   108	  (`masked_trig_products_completed_paper`,
   109	  `masked_continuous_wave_completed_paper`). `P:frequency-row` and
   110	  `C:frequency-time` are stated with the section's hypotheses (`H:homog`
   111	  with `a = alpha0`, the range of `gamma`, and of `beta` for the corollary)
   112	  by `frequency_row_paper` and `frequency_time_paper`, with the constant
   113	  chosen before `d, Gamma, mu, nu, C, h`. `L:occupation-kernel-row` and
   114	  `L:spatial-physical-pair` are stated with the section's hypotheses
   115	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `D = q - 2a`) by `occupation_kernel_row_paper`
   116	  and `spatial_physical_pair_paper`. `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` is stated
   117	  with the manuscript's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`) by
   118	  `masked_auxiliary_norm_paper`; its clause for a real `H` after
   119	  complexification is not formalized, and `E:masked-hilbert-fourier` is
   120	  proved for any complex Banach space. `L:variational-heat-envelope` and the
   121	  display of `L:variational-global-mean` are stated with the section's
   122	  hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
   123	  `variational_heat_envelope_paper` and `variational_global_mean_paper`; the
   124	  latter's first sentence (all mixed derivatives bounded) is not formalized.
   125	  `L:phase-bessel` is proved for any measure space and any complete complex
   126	  inner product space and stated with the manuscript's hypotheses by
   127	  `phase_bessel_paper` (separability carried and not used).
   128	  `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` is stated with the proposition's
   129	  hypotheses by `masked_quotient_obstruction_paper`, which also proves that
   130	  `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2` satisfies `H:homog` (with `alpha = 1`) and
   131	  `Gamma != 0`; `E W(F)^2` is read as the covariance functional of `E:cov`
   132	  (the noise is not constructed). The Rayleigh-form part of
   133	  `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (a uniform positive floor, the Lipschitz
   134	  bounds and `0 < I_Psi < infinity`, for the rate defined by
   135	  `E:variational-real-rayleigh`) is stated with the section's hypotheses by
   136	  `variational_unmasked_rate_paper`; its operator half (`H_s` self-adjoint,
   137	  `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`) is not formalized. `L:spatial-static-controls` and
   138	  `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` are stated with the section's hypotheses
   139	  (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by
   140	  `spatial_static_controls_completed_paper` and
   141	  `spatial_smooth_ratio_completed_paper` (`SpatialOccupationCompleted`),
   142	  with the score displays `E:spatial-static-score` and
   143	  `E:spatial-smooth-score` in an existential form and their supremum forms
   144	  on the named input `S1Bdd` (see "Not in Lean"); `R_0` is positive and
   145	  finite with nothing supplied, by the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <=
   146	  2^(1+alpha) R_Gamma(1) b(g)^(alpha/2)` of `SpatialFourierBound`, so `R_0 <
   147	  infinity` does not depend on `T:full-upper` (the TeX derives it from the
   148	  finiteness of `S_1^pos`). `L:positive-series-type` is stated with the
   149	  lemma's hypotheses by `positive_series_type_paper`.
   150	  `C:white-relative-width` and `L:white-clock-laplace` are stated with the
   151	  section's hypotheses by `white_relative_width_paper` and
   152	  `white_clock_laplace_paper`, the latter with the damping parameters
   153	  `eta_1, eta_2 > 0` of `E:white-self-clock-transform` made explicit (the
   154	  TeX gives them no sign). `L:inventory-product` is stated with the
   155	  section's hypothesis `H:homog` by `inventory_product_paper`, with the
   156	  explicit constant `inventoryConst alpha alpha0` fixed before `M` and `k`.
   157	  `P:spatial-four-linear` and `P:spatial-energy-map` are stated with the
   158	  section's hypotheses (`H:homog`, `Gamma != 0`, `a = alpha0`) by the
   159	  `_completed` wrappers of `SpatialOccupationL7Completed` (for example
   160	  `spatial_four_linear_paper_completed` and
   161	  `spatial_energy_value_paper_completed`), which discharge the density of
   162	  test functions in `H^1` (the input `hdense` of `SpatialFourLinear`) with

   164	  sequential form, and `E:spatial-static-energy-score` in the existential
   165	  form, its supremum form on the named input `S1Bdd`.
   166	  `P:occupation-physical-class` is stated with the section's hypotheses and
   167	  the TeX's constants `R_sp` and `E_sp` by
   168	  `occupation_physical_class_Esp_paper` (`SquarePairingBounds` discharged by

   170	  measurable representatives of `g` and `grad g`; the construction of such
   171	  representatives from strong `H^1`-measurability is not formalized. Five
   172	  further results are formalized with every conclusion proved but with
   173	  analytic inputs supplied as named hypotheses: `P:radius-mean-anchor` (the

  3540	
  3541	Elementary scalar facts that `notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex`
  3542	(main file, at `975feb3`) uses inline inside proofs, plus one standalone
  3543	Gamma-function tool (`gamma_mid_sq_le`) for which no manuscript line is
  3544	claimed. None of them is a labelled result. Everything is proved and nothing is supplied as a
  3545	hypothesis. The module contains:
  3546	
  3547	- the finite `ell^nu` inequality `sum a_k^nu <= (sum a_k)^nu` for `nu >= 1`
  3548	  and `a_k >= 0`;
  3549	- the series bound `S_nu(x) = sum_k x^k/(k!)^nu <= exp(nu x^(1/nu))` for
  3550	  `nu >= 1` and `x >= 0`, with summability as part of the conclusion (a Lean
  3551	  `tsum` of a non-summable family is `0`);
  3552	- the `beta < 1` Hoelder variant of the proof of `P:static-phase-all-orders`
  3553	  (lines 2597-2606): `sum x^n/(n!)^beta <= 2^(1-beta) exp(2 beta x^(1/beta))`
  3554	  for `1/2 <= beta < 1`, proved by the TeX's own Hoelder factorization, and
  3555	  the displayed bound `<= 2 e^(3x^(1/beta))` for every `1/2 <= beta <= 3`;
  3556	  the TeX needs it only at `beta = (3-alpha)/2 in (1/2, 3/2)`;
  3557	- `(k!)^2 <= r! s!` when `r + s = 2k` (lines 2681, 5046);
  3558	- the two-sided bound `k log k - k + 1 <= log k! <= k log k - k + 1 + log k`
  3559	  for `k >= 1`, a step of the proof of `L:positive-series-type`
  3560	  (lines 7171-7174);
  3561	- `Gamma((x+y)/2)^2 <= Gamma(x) Gamma(y)` (the standalone tool; its row has

  3563	  tool, no manuscript line claimed)").

  2458	\begin{lemma}[Exact cutoffs for finite Gaussian words]\label{L:finite-word-cutoff}
  2459	  Let $g_{ij}$, $1 \le i \le M$, $1 \le j \le m_i$, be independent standard real
  2460	  Gaussian coordinates, grouped by color $i$, and let $\mathscr{X}$ be a complex
  2461	  Hilbert space. On Gaussian polynomials with coefficients in $\mathscr{X}$ set
  2462	  \[
  2463	    J_i=\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}M_{g_{ij}}\otimes K_{ij},
  2464	  \]
  2465	  where each $K_{ij}$ is bounded on $\mathscr{X}$. Let $F_0,\ldots,F_n$ be
  2466	  bounded operators acting only on $\mathscr{X}$. Fix a word $i_1,\ldots,i_n$,
  2467	  and let $r_i$ be the number of its occurrences of color $i$. If $N_i \ge r_i$
  2468	  and $P$ projects each color onto total Hermite degree at most $N_i$, then, for
  2469	  every $v \in \mathscr{X}$,
  2470	  \begin{equation}\label{E:finite-word-cutoff}
  2471	    \begin{split}
  2472	      &(I\otimes F_n)(PJ_{i_n}P)(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2473	      (PJ_{i_1}P)(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v)\\
  2474	      &\qquad=(I\otimes F_n)J_{i_n}(I\otimes F_{n-1})\cdots
  2475	      J_{i_1}(I\otimes F_0)(1\otimes v).
  2476	    \end{split}
  2477	  \end{equation}
  2478	  The equality holds for finite sums and for Bochner integrals of such words
  2479	  whenever the displayed vector integrals exist.
  2480	\end{lemma}
